title: Days Set Aside From an Overdue Stretch on Equipment Rental and Demo Kit Where the Household Is Staying With the Collective
content:
A household still in one of the collective's own beds has not taken the kit home with it, and days of the overdue stretch on an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement are set aside accordingly.

## The rule

Where the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season whose departure date falls after the date written on the agreement, the days from the day after the date written on the agreement through that departure date are set aside.

Where the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season whose departure date falls on or before the date written on the agreement, the travel day relief is set aside instead. The travel day relief is 1 day.

In any other case no day is set aside under this heading.

## The branches

| Resort Lodging reservation held for the season | Its departure date against the date written on the agreement | Days set aside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | after it | from the day after the date written on the agreement through the departure date |
| yes | on it | 1 |
| yes | before it | 1 |
| no | — | none under this heading |

A departure date falling on the date written on the agreement is not after it, so it takes the travel day relief of 1 day rather than a run of days.

## Worked counts on hypothetical dates

Take an agreement written to a due date of the 10th of January.

- The household's lodging reservation shows a departure date of the 13th of January: the 11th, 12th and 13th are set aside, which is 3 days.
- The departure date is the 10th of January: the travel day relief of 1 day is set aside.
- The departure date is the 6th of January: the travel day relief of 1 day is set aside.
- The household holds no lodging reservation for the season: no day is set aside under this heading.

## Point of judgement

**Which reservation is read.** The reservation read is one held by the household with Resort Lodging for the season the agreement belongs to, and the date read from it is its departure date.
